summary: Try Thai suki (สุกี้ไทย) in Yaowarat as a single-serve noodle dish: suki nam is glass noodles, vegetables and protein in broth; suki haeng is the wok-fried version. Michelin describes a fermented-tofu and sesame-based sauce as the key Thai flavour. Tai Heng at 67/4 Yaowarat 8 is a promising specific stop for Hainanese-style suki, including dry suki cooked with its seasoned marinade and served with fermented-tofu dipping sauce.
whyGo: Compare the soup and dry versions of a familiar Bangkok dish shaped by Chinese and Japanese influences.
At Tai Heng, try a distinctly Hainanese Yaowarat preparation, rather than assuming all Thai suki tastes the same.
The meal fits neatly into a Chinatown food walk and the nearby Wat Mangkon MRT station makes the area straightforward to reach.
bestFor: Travellers curious about Bangkok's everyday Thai-Chinese food
People who enjoy glass noodles, vegetables, meat or seafood and punchy fermented-tofu sauce
A daytime lunch stop in Yaowarat
skipIf: You need a reliably vegetarian, vegan or allergen-safe meal without confirming ingredients and kitchen practices
You require guaranteed step-free access or accessible toilets at the restaurant
You want a Japanese-style communal hot pot: Thai suki is commonly served as an individual noodle dish
duration: Allow 45–75 minutes for a meal and a short walk around Yaowarat; this is a planning estimate, with queue time varying.
cost: No current Tai Heng menu price was verified. Allow roughly THB 100–250 per person for a dish and drink as a planning estimate, then check the menu before ordering.
hours: A Bangkok Biz News feature dated 7 October 2026 reports Tai Heng open daily except Sunday, 10:00–17:00, and lists contact numbers +66 2 222 6791 and +66 93 656 5366. Reconfirm before travelling.
bestTime: Go for an early lunch or mid-afternoon, within Tai Heng's reported daytime hours. If the shop is closed or full, Yaowarat has other suki options; check each venue's current schedule.
gettingThere: Take the MRT Blue Line to Wat Mangkon. BEM lists Exit 1 for Yaowarat Road and Phadung Dao Road; follow Yaowarat Soi 8 (Trok Tao) to Tai Heng at 67/4. Check a current map for the final turn through the lanes.
booking: Treat Tai Heng as a casual walk-in restaurant; no booking channel was verified. The recent feature lists phone numbers, so call to confirm opening and availability, especially near public holidays.
accessibility: BEM lists elevators and ramps at Wat Mangkon station exits. Step-free continuity through the Yaowarat lanes, restaurant entry, seating clearance and toilets at Tai Heng were not verified; contact the restaurant if these matter.
practicalTips: Ask for suki nam (สุกี้น้ำ) for the soup version or suki haeng (สุกี้แห้ง) for the wok-fried version.
Tai Heng's dry suki is seasoned during cooking and accompanied by its fermented-tofu dipping sauce; ask staff if you want the sauce kept separate.
Recipes commonly include meat or seafood, egg, soy-based seasonings and fermented tofu. Confirm ingredients and cross-contact directly for dietary restrictions.
Tai Heng also serves Hainanese chicken rice, useful if your group wants different dishes.
decemberNotes: Thai suki is a year-round dish, and no special December 2026 event or schedule was found. Tai Heng's reported hours are daytime only and exclude Sunday; holiday hours may differ, so confirm by phone before making a special trip.
uncertainties: Tai Heng's reported 10:00–17:00 hours come from a recent news feature rather than a restaurant-operated booking or hours page; confirm for your date.
